design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 1 (service_repair_orders, env_0075) — design dossier.

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 -> prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[5,4,6,6]. Assignment: service_ext_comeback_labor_credit 5, service_ext_diagnostic_credit 4, service_ext_early_payment_discount 6, service_ext_repeat_repair_estimate 6 (multiset {4,5,6,6} = draw).

[Why this is a good test] A fleet manager asks one thing: take the diagnostic charge off the Silverado's Fairborn repair order RO 261109. The scored root number (the 76.36 diagnostic credit) is the product of (a) a 4-factor fleet diagnostic-credit schedule (credit share scaled by the twelve-month spend for a major repair, away-store share keyed on the Kessler Care plan, decision-speed share, payment-standing share), (b) two prerequisites the opening world leaves unmet: no authorized estimate decision stands on RO 261109 line A (so no credit at all is owed yet), and the F-250 invoice RO 261030 was paid by ACH inside its 15-day window without its early-payment discount (so the twelve-month spend is overstated), and (c) a discount that is itself wrong unless the comeback credit owed on that same invoice is booked first (RO 261030 repeats the F-250's EGR repair RO 260205 inside the 12-month / 12,000-mile repair warranty). The estimate the customer authorizes in person is a 6-factor computation of its own (rate lock, diagnosis-overlap hours, repeat allowance, maintained-vehicle allowance, parts price index, parts volume discount). Difficulty comes from reading four policies' prerequisite sentences, reconciling 59 ledger rows and 6 authorization records across 14 repair orders and ten units, and reading two other products (purchase deals, maintenance plans); nothing is hidden behind a tool choice — each problem has one tool and the tool validates nothing.

[Scope snapshot] Occupied by task 0: service_ext_estimate_overage_credit, service_ext_paid_ro_points, service_ext_month_end_points_expiry, service_ext_owner_points_redemption and their four tools (retail Owner Rewards: overage credit, points earning, expiry, redemption). Claimed by task 1 (the last task, M=2): service_ext_comeback_labor_credit (credit_comeback_labor_f15915d4), service_ext_early_payment_discount (credit_early_payment_discount_b0e7362c), service_ext_repeat_repair_estimate (authorize_repair_estimate_690e2aa2, owner=user), service_ext_diagnostic_credit (credit_diagnostic_fee_eae01e67). These are the fleet-account surfaces (comeback, net-terms discount, estimate authorization, diagnostic credit) none of which task 0 touches; the two scopes are disjoint and together cover all 8 extended policies. No headroom is left to reserve (M=2).

[Problem-tree card]
root a = service_ext_diagnostic_credit (agent tool credit_diagnostic_fee_eae01e67).
edge a <- b, value_input, gate authorized_estimate, form state. Sentence (a's own rule, negated direction): "A diagnostic credit on a line whose vehicle carries an earlier customer-pay parts repair, with a customer-pay labor charge on its line and its store repair warranty ended by the diagnosis date, is not booked until the records carry the customer's authorized decision on the written estimate for the same concern line." Condition: the diagnosed line carries an authorized decision dated within the window. Opening: RO 261109 line A has no decision row (initial_state.service_repair_authorizations holds rows for RO 250312, RO 260205 A/B, RO 260302, RO 260521, RO 260915 only). Only write in the difficulty bringing it about: authorize_repair_estimate_690e2aa2 (b's target tool; the only tool that writes an estimate decision). Resolver owner: user (the authorization is the customer's own decision under service_evt_estimate). Deletion: a = 0 (no credit owed) instead of 76.36.
edge a <- g, value_input, gate spend_12m, form state. Sentence (a's rule, affirmative): "The diagnostic credit is fixed only after the records carry the early-payment discount owed on every fleet invoice of the account paid in full inside its discount window whose customer-pay labor charges exceed the comeback, estimate overage and goodwill credits on it by at least ten dollars." Opening: RO 261030 paid 2026-11-11 by ACH (12 days after 2026-10-30) with no early_payment_discount credit. Only writer of an early_payment_discount credit: credit_early_payment_discount_b0e7362c. Deletion: a = 76.38 instead of 76.36.
edge g <- c, value_input, gate invoice_credits, form state. Sentence (g's rule, negated): "The early-payment discount on an invoice is not fixed until the records carry the comeback credit owed on every repeat repair on that invoice that falls inside the repair warranty and whose original repair line carries a customer-pay labor charge." Opening: RO 261030 line A labor 832.66 (F-250, 50,100 mi, no parts) repeats RO 260205 line A (2026-02-02, 38,500 mi) inside the warranty; no comeback_repair credit. Only writer of a comeback_repair credit: credit_comeback_labor_f15915d4. Deletion: g = 15.18 instead of 3.89.
Directions: a<-b negated ("not booked until"), a<-g affirmative ("fixed only after"), g<-c negated ("not fixed until") — a credit desk says a credit is "not booked until" its authorization stands and a figure is "fixed only after" its inputs are posted; the charter carries both directions. Four-point test: each sentence joins the policy's own result to a record-visible state with an ordering connective, names no tool, id or code token, and states exactly the scope of its condition (every invoice paid inside its window; every repeat repair inside the warranty on that invoice; the same concern line).
Topological order c, g, b, a (b parallel to c/g; both orders replayed identical). Value_input edges 3 of 3 (floor max(3-1,1)=2). User write: b.

[Base-invariant card]
service_evt_comeback in the estimate (round 3): the estimate policy prices nothing for a failure inside the store repair warranty of the earlier repair (that failure is a comeback whose parts are not billed); RO 250312's warranty ended 2026-03-12, before the diagnosis, and the diagnostic credit's wait on the authorization applies only to such out-of-warranty repeats.
service_evt_diagnostic window — the base sentence "A diagnostic credit is given only when the repair is authorized within diagnostic_credit_window_days calendar days after the diagnosis date." is retired on every account by the diagnostic credit policy's declared overwrite and replaced by its own sentence: the repair counts as authorized on the date of the latest authorized decision on the diagnosed line (a later decision supersedes an earlier one) and the credit is given only when that date falls within the window, the diagnosis date being day 0. Anchor: line_date of the diagnostic fee row RO 261109 A = 2026-11-09 (day 0); Net 30 window 30 calendar days -> last day 2026-12-09. At frozen_time (2026-11-18) false (no decision); after step 15 true (decided 2026-11-18, day 9). Just-inside case: decision 2026-12-09; just-outside: 2026-12-10. The once-only, declined and waived-when-covered sentences stay in force; the turbo repair is customer pay under service_combo_coverage_priority (no recall, warranty or service contract covers it; the Kessler Care Fleet plan covers maintenance visits only), so no coverage source pays any part of the line and the waived-when-covered clause has no reading here.
service_evt_diagnostic.one_diagnostic_credit — no credit row points at the RO 261109 diagnostic fee at the opening; step 17 books the only one.
service_evt_comeback.within_repair_warranty — original RO 260205 line A 2026-02-02 + 12 calendar months = 2027-02-02; 38,500 + 12,000 = 50,500 miles; repeat 2026-10-30 at 50,100 miles is inside both (just-inside: 2027-02-02 at 50,500; just-outside: 2027-02-03 or 50,501). For the Silverado, RO 250312 (2025-03-12) + 12 months = 2026-03-12, so the 2026-11-09 turbo failure is outside the warranty and is customer pay (why b prices an estimate rather than a comeback).
service_evt_estimate.line_authorized — work above 25.00 is billed only on an authorized line; a Net 30 fleet preauthorizes lines up to 1,500.00, and the 2,847.19 turbo estimate exceeds that, so a separate customer decision is needed (b, owner=user). RO 261030 line A (832.66 billed, labor only) sat under the preauthorized limit.
service_evt_payment_terms — fleet invoice due line date + 30 days; RO 261030 paid in full 2026-11-11; the only open item is the 165.00 diagnostic fee dated 2026-11-09 (due 2026-12-09), so no late fee and no credit hold is owed at frozen_time. Overwritten clause (the base early-payment sentence) is replaced by g's self-scoped sentence, which still credits as early_payment_discount, rounds to the cent and denies a partial payment.
service_evt_comeback overwrite — c's replaced_by names its scope (commercial fleet accounts), restates that on every account the replacement parts of a comeback are not billed and that any other account keeps comeback_labor_covered_pct.
service_evt_diagnostic overwrite — a's replaced_by names its scope (commercial fleet accounts) and keeps the base credit at diagnostic_credit_pct for every other account.

[Business-object card]
c: object = the repeat labor charge of RO 261030 line A (service_line_id in initial_state, the only service_labor_charged row on RO 261030); original = RO 260205 line A (labor 885.36, parts 1,530.45); excluded: RO 260205 line B (declined 214.60, never billed — counted only by the declined-work share), RO 261030 shop fees (not labor), RO 260302 / RO 251204 on the F-350 (another unit). Tool writes source_line_id = the RO 261030 labor row.
g: object = invoice RO 261030 (labor 832.66, shop supplies 35.00, hazardous waste 4.95, payment 872.61); credits on it after step 11: the comeback 645.54 (labor share plus the refunded 35.00 and 4.95 fees). Excluded: the 2026-03-06 late-fee payment (no repair order). Tool writes source_line_id = the RO 261030 labor row.
b: object = RO 261109 line A (Silverado, KCF, 78,400 mi); earlier repair = RO 250312 line A (KCV, 9.8 h at 158.00, parts list 2,860.00, 61,200 mi). Excluded: any other unit's parts charges (keyed on vehicle_id).
a: object = the RO 261109 line A diagnostic fee row (165.00); authorized estimate = the step 15 decision. Tool writes source_line_id = the diagnostic fee row.

[Factor card — values from the executed sensitivity run (round 3 replay on the handling-time worlds)]
c comeback credit = 645.54; all-baseline (repeat labor x comeback_labor_covered_pct 1.00) = 832.66. Gate: 2026-10-30 is on or before 2027-02-02 and 50,100 <= 38,500 + 12,000, original RO 260205 is another repair order -> owed.
 aged_repair_share (parameter; >= 9 whole months 0.70 / 6-8 whole months 0.80 / else 1.00): 8 whole months -> 0.80; baseline 796.93. Near-miss: counted to the November call the original would be 9 months old; the rule counts to the repeat labor charge.
 original_store_basis (method; another store -> the original labor charge / same store and the repeat labor larger -> the original labor plus half the excess / else the repeat labor charge): RO 260205 at Kessler Ford Springfield, RO 261030 at Kessler Commercial Vehicle Center -> 885.36; baseline 832.66 gives 609.49. All pairs: tier 1 vs 3 differ whenever the two labor charges differ; tier 2 vs 1 and vs 3 differ on tier 2's whole domain (repeat > original gives a value strictly between them) - a different combination of the two inputs, not a rate swap.
 wear_deduction_rule (parameter, cross maintenance; > 8,000 mi and no plan 0.15 / > 8,000 mi and plan 0.05 / else 0): 11,600 mi, plan KC-2409266 active on the F-250 -> 0.05; baseline 677.41. Multi-source.
 declined_work_share (parameter; declined decision >= 500.00 -> 0.85 / declined decisions all below 500.00 -> 0.90 / else 1): line B declined at 214.60 -> 0.90; baseline 712.82.
 repeat_fee_refund (method; original RO carried a shop supplies and a hazardous waste fee -> the repeat's shop supplies and hazardous waste fees are added / original carried a shop supplies fee only -> the repeat's shop supplies fee is added / else nothing): RO 260205 carried both -> 35.00 + 4.95 = 39.95; baseline 605.59. A comeback redoes a job whose fees the customer already paid once, so the redo's fees of the same kinds are refunded with the labor (an added input, not a rate).
 885.36 x 0.80 x (1 - 0.05) x 0.90 + 39.95 = 645.536 -> 645.54.
g early-payment discount = 3.89 (handling world after c); all-baseline 0 (12 days > 10-day base window); an invoice whose customer-pay labor exceeds its credits by less than 10.00 earns none.
 ach_window_rule (parameter): ACH, Net 30 -> 15 days; baseline 0. Near-miss: 12 days fails the base 10-day window.
 fleet_deal_rate (parameter, cross purchase): F-250 deal KCV-22-20417 -> 0.025; baseline 3.33.
 prompt_payer_addition (parameter): 12 payments in the last twelve whole months (the 2025-11-03 check excluded) -> +0.005; baseline 3.33.
 account_tenure_addition (parameter): 70 whole months -> +0.005; baseline 3.33.
 discountable_base_rule (method, cross maintenance): ACH and the F-250's plan -> 832.66 + 0 + 35.00 - 645.54 = 222.12; baseline 187.12 gives 3.27.
 payment_standing_share (parameter; late fee and no returned payment 0.5 / returned payment 0.25 / else 1): late fee 2026-02-27 -> 0.5; baseline 7.77.
 (0.025 + 0.005 + 0.005) x 222.12 x 0.5 = 3.887 -> 3.89.
b repeat-repair estimate = 2847.19; all-baseline 3719.65. Scope: the Silverado's earlier repair RO 250312 (2025-03-12, 61,200 mi) is outside the store repair warranty at the 2026-11-09 diagnosis (ended 2026-03-12), so the failure is not a comeback and the estimate is priced.
 rate_lock_rule (parameter: the tier selects which posted rate is used): estimate at KCF (away), earlier at KCV (home) -> 158.00; baseline 165.00 gives 2870.23.
 diagnosis_overlap_hours (method): 1.0 diagnostic hour, single earlier labor charge -> 8.8 h; baseline 9.8 gives 2906.28.
 repeat_labor_allowance (parameter): 19 whole months and 17,200 miles -> 0.5; baseline 3367.20.
 maintained_vehicle_allowance (parameter, cross maintenance): plan KC-2404183 active, 17,200 > 15,000 mi -> 0.88; baseline 2918.10. Multi-source.
 parts_price_index (parameter): 19 whole months (12-23) -> +0.03; baseline 2779.41.
 parts_volume_discount (parameter): 12-month customer-pay parts 7,822.77 -> 0.03 more; baseline 2935.57. Near-miss: adding the out-of-window RO 250312 and RO 251204 parts gives 10,566.65 and the 0.05 tier.
 labor 1181.84 x 0.5 x 0.88 = 520.01; parts 2860 x 1.03 x (1 - 0.18 - 0.03) = 2327.18; 2847.19.
a diagnostic credit = 76.36 (world after c, g, b); all-baseline 165.00.
 spend_scaled_share (method): estimate 2,847.19 >= 1,500 and twelve-month spend 14,362.16 - 645.54 - 3.89 = 13,712.73 < 15,000 -> 0.914182; baseline 83.53. Near-miss: RO 251204 (2025-10-08) is outside twelve whole months.
 away_store_share_rule (parameter, cross maintenance): KCF away from home, the Silverado's plan active -> 0.9; baseline 84.85.
 decision_speed_share (parameter): 9 days -> 0.75; baseline 101.82.
 diagnostic_standing_share (parameter): late fee, no returned payment -> 0.75; baseline 101.82.
 165.00 x 0.914182 x 0.9 x 0.75 x 0.75 = 76.362 -> 76.36.
Cross-difficulty evidence seeded: purchase_deals KCV-22-20417 (F-250, KCV) and KCF-21-21388 (Silverado, Kessler Chevrolet Fairborn), both Fleet Vehicle Purchase Agreement, closed; maintenance_plans KC-2409266 (F-250) and KC-2404183 (Silverado), Kessler Care Fleet 12-Visit, active. No stamp names any tier.

[Seed design] Hollister Landscape & Snow LLC (fleet_business, profile 2021-01-11), ten registered units with valid 17-character VINs (serials beginning 2), Commercial Fleet Account - Net 30 SA-258430 at KCV, credit limit 25,000.00. Fourteen repair orders 2025-03 to 2026-11, each priced by base: labor = hours x store posted rate less 15% (cap 1,000), parts = list less 18%, shop supplies 5% of discounted labor capped 35.00, hazardous waste 4.95 on fluid jobs, every invoice paid in full by ACH or check (all but RO 261030 after the 15-day ACH window, so no other discount is owed); one late fee (RO 260117, 25.00 minimum, 2026-02-27, paid 2026-03-06). Authorizations: lines above 1,500.00 carry an authorized decision rounded up to the next ten dollars of the billed amount; RO 260205 line B declined. Load-bearing rows: RO 261030 labor/payment (c, g), RO 260205 (c), RO 250312 (b), RO 261109 diagnostic fee (b, a), the late fee (g, a), the payments (g), the deals and plans (c, g, b, a). Automatic clauses checked: no invoice past due (no late fee owed at frozen_time), no credit hold, no other repeat inside a warranty (the F-350 and Transit repeats each bill their own parts, so their own repair order is the latest parts repair and no comeback is owed), fleet tiers earn no points, no other invoice paid inside its window; the deals are closed and the plans in term, so nothing in another product is owed.

[Persona] Greg Eberly, brisk fleet manager; volunteers the business name, the Silverado, the Fairborn store and the wish to have the diagnostic charge taken off; gives phone 9375552618 and EIN last four 2953 (ZIP 45324, email as fallbacks) when asked; reads RO 261109 off the advisor's text only when asked; describes the truck only when asked. He knows the advisor has diagnosed a repeat turbo failure and that the repair still needs the company's approval; he knows no estimate figure. Passive branches: if told the charge comes off only once the repair is approved, he approves the estimate himself at the amount the desk quotes (authority up to 5,000.00) and completes the handed-over approval for RO 261109 line A; if told something else must be posted first, he lets the desk proceed; he closes when told the diagnostic credit is applied. He makes no payment and never mentions the F-250, a comeback or a discount.

[Standard solution] find_customers -> verify_customer_identity -> find_service_accounts -> find_service_ro_lines -> find_service_repair_authorizations -> find_vehicles -> find_stores -> find_purchase_deals -> find_maintenance_plans -> find_maintenance_plan_ledger; read the diagnostic credit rule (two waits), see no decision on RO 261109 A (the Silverado's earlier repair is outside its warranty, so the wait applies) and RO 261030 paid inside its ACH window with no discount; read the discount rule's wait and find the comeback owed on RO 261030; book c 645.54, then g 3.89, hand over the estimate authorization (2847.19) for RO 261109 line A, then book a 76.36.

[Verification] Round-3 replay (scratch, deleted after use) runs the gold through the real tools and evaluates each policy with check_compute's DSL on the handling-time world: c 645.54, g 3.89, b 2847.19, a 76.36; all-baseline 832.66 / 0 / 3719.65 / 165.00; skip runs g<-c 15.18, a<-g 76.38, a<-b 0; order b, c, g, a gives identical terminal tables. Unrounded values (645.536, 3.887, 2847.1916, 76.362) are not half-cent ties; every money RND is RND(x + 0.000000001, 2), half up like the tools.

[Closure] policy -> tool -> computation step/arg -> GT call: c -> credit_comeback_labor_f15915d4 -> step 11 credit_amount; g -> credit_early_payment_discount_b0e7362c -> step 13 credit_amount; b -> authorize_repair_estimate_690e2aa2 (user) -> step 15 estimate_amount; a -> credit_diagnostic_fee_eae01e67 -> step 17 credit_amount. required_documents = charter_scope.extended_policies = [c, g, b, a]. Events written: service_line_credited (comeback_repair, early_payment_discount, diagnostic_applied_to_repair; base triggers []) and one service_repair_authorizations intake row; none lands in another category; every money row > 0.00, enforced in the tool bodies.

[Revisions] (1) c's covered labor share had a Platinum tier and its declined-work share a retail tier that the policy's own fleet-only scope can never reach -> ladders rewritten as an age schedule (>= 9 months 0.70 / 6-8 months 0.80 / else 1.00) and a declined-amount schedule (>= 500.00 0.85 / below 0.90 / else 1); result unchanged 575.31. (2) c's replaced_by now restates that on every account the comeback's replacement parts are not billed (recipe C13). (3) c's credit basis dropped an unstated 'original labor > 0' guard (rule == compute). (4) 'standing share' was the same quantity name in g and a -> renamed 'discount standing share' (g) and 'diagnostic standing share' / 'diagnostic credit share' (a). (5) The Silverado's purchase deal moved from KCV (a Ford franchise) to Kessler Chevrolet Fairborn (KCF-21-21388), so a new Chevrolet is sold by a Chevrolet store; persona updated.

[Revisions r2] (audit revision_1) C-3/C-8: the comeback credit's store basis tier 2 (same store, repeat larger -> lesser of the two) selected the same amount as tier 1 and is now 'same store and the posted rate changed -> the repeat's hours at the original posted rate'; the duty share (keyed on how the unit was bought) is replaced by the fleet downtime allowance (6.0+ hours 100.00 / 3.0-5.9 hours 50.00 / else 0); comeback credit 575.31 -> 705.59, discount 5.12 -> 2.84, diagnostic credit 76.75 -> 76.03. C-4/C-8: the estimate's parts warranty share (a split payer against service_combo_coverage_priority, keyed on the installing store) is replaced by the parts volume discount on the account's twelve-month customer-pay parts; estimate 1,739.61 -> 2,859.01. C-1: the comeback and diagnostic credit policies price every other account exactly as the restated base (repeat labor x comeback_labor_covered_pct; diagnostic fee x diagnostic_credit_pct where diagnostic_credit_on_repair), the factor sentences are written 'On a commercial fleet account'. C-7b: the comeback compute now tests the repair warranty (months by the base anchor rule, miles inclusive). C-7c: the diagnostic credit policy declares an overwrite of the base window sentence on every account: the latest authorized decision on the line is the operative authorization. C-6: the diagnostic credit tool docstring no longer says 'once ... authorized'. C-9: the estimate's store and the diagnostic credit's vehicle are named only in the factor sentences that use them. C-10: every 'last twelve whole months' window states its rolling convention, so the credits dated today count in the twelve-month spend and the a<-g edge bears weight (76.05 -> 76.03). C-2: generic assembly sentences. C-7d: tie rule stated. Persona: no longer claims a written estimate figure exists. Absent-record guards: every policy states that with no reviewed object (no payment, no diagnostic fee, no earlier parts repair) it books or prices nothing, and the compute returns 0 there instead of failing (probe run: no payments -> comeback 0, discount 0; no diagnostic fee -> estimate 0, credit 0; no parts -> comeback 0, estimate 0). Decoys probed: cancelled deals -> fleet_deal_rate falls through (discount 13.01 on the opening world); expired plans -> wear 0.15, discountable base without supplies, maintained allowance 1, away share 0.75; none crash. Whole months: a whole month falling on a day the later month lacks completes on the first day of the month after, stated in every rule. The T1 values are unchanged by these guards.

[Revisions r3] (audit revision_2) N-2: the fleet downtime allowance (lost-time compensation, which the blueprint sends to a human) is removed and replaced by repeat_fee_refund (the redo's shop fees of the kinds the original job already paid are refunded with the labor); comeback credit 705.59 -> 645.54, discount 2.84 -> 3.89, diagnostic credit 76.03 -> 76.36. N-4: the store basis tier 2 is now the original labor plus half the excess (a combination of the two labor charges, not a rate swap); rate_lock_rule is labelled parameter (its tiers select which posted rate is used), so the estimate's methods are diagnosis_overlap_hours and no tier swaps a multiplier under a method label. N-3: the estimate policy prices nothing for a failure inside the earlier repair's store warranty (base comeback rule honoured); the diagnostic credit's wait on the authorization is carved to repeats whose warranty has ended. Zero-amount edges: the comeback credit (when owed) and the early-payment discount (paid in full inside the window) are never less than one cent; the returned-payment share is 0.25 instead of 0, so no waited-on write can compute 0.00 and be refused. N-5: tool bodies enforce the line letter set, the source row's line, numeric parsing of points and amounts, and the module docstring states this. Rounding: RND(x + 0.000001, 2). The persona and initial_state are unchanged.

[Revisions r4] (audit revision_3: task 1 PASS kept; coordinator rulings) R-3: the one-cent floors are gone. The comeback credit owes nothing where the paid repair order carries no customer-pay labor charge, and on a fleet account nothing against an original repair line without a customer-pay labor charge (a parts sale); the discount's wait on it is carved to repeats whose original line carries such a charge (RO 260205 line A: 885.36, inside the wait). The discount gives nothing where the invoice's customer-pay labor exceeds its comeback, overage and goodwill credits by less than 10.00 (so any discount given is at least 0.025 before rounding), and the diagnostic credit's wait on it is carved to fleet invoices at or above that margin (RO 261030: 832.66 - 645.54 = 187.12, inside the wait). Values unchanged: 645.54 / 3.89 / 76.36. Rounding ruling: the factor-sensitivity figure of diagnosis_overlap_hours (2919.445) sat exactly on a half cent, so maintained_share_high is now 0.88 (was 0.9): estimate 1181.84 x 0.5 x 0.88 + 2860 x 1.03 x 0.79 = 520.0096 + 2327.182 = 2847.1916 -> 2847.19; sensitivities 2870.23 / 2906.28 / 3367.20 / 2918.10 / 2779.41 / 2935.57, all-baseline 3719.65; the diagnostic credit is unchanged (the estimate stays above 1,500). Every scored, baseline and sensitivity figure now sits more than 1e-6 from a half cent (smallest distance 0.0004, discountable_base_rule 3.2746). RND(x + 0.000000001, 2); exact decimal half-up tools (R-2).

[Revisions r5] (audit revision_4, R-4) The parts-sale test now holds on every account: the comeback credit's rule reads 'On every account, an original repair line that carries no customer-pay labor charge is a parts sale rather than a repair the store performed, carries no repair warranty, and no comeback credit is owed against it', and the compute folds original_labor > 0 into in_warranty, so the retail branch (repeat labor x comeback_labor_covered_pct) no longer credits a repeat of a parts-only sale. Class sweep: the repeat-repair estimate prices nothing where the earlier line carries no customer-pay labor charge (a parts sale, not a repair), and the diagnostic credit's wait on the authorization is carved to earlier repairs with a customer-pay labor charge on their line. Probes: Gold account with a parts-only counter sale then a paid labor repair order -> comeback 0 (was 154.80); same world on Net 30 -> 0; Silverado earlier line without labor -> estimate 0. Task values unchanged: 645.54 / 3.89 / 2847.19 / 76.36 (RO 260205 line A carries 885.36 of labor; RO 250312 line A carries labor).

[Revisions r6] (render_source render_r1 F1-F4) F1/F2: the paid-in-full balance of the points rule and of the discount now counts every charge on the repair order, customer-pay and deductible alike, in rule ('its charges, customer-pay and deductible alike') and compute (labor and parts sums without a pay_type filter); probe: an unpaid 100.00 deductible on RO 261030 -> discount 0. F3: the comeback rule names one row - 'the repeat labor charge is its latest customer-pay labor charge' - and compute reads that row (amount, date, odometer, store, unit all from the latest customer-pay labor charge; the tie rule picks the one listed first); the original repair's labor is stated as the total of the customer-pay labor charges on its line; the discount and the overage credit are booked against the latest customer-pay labor charge; the estimate's earlier repair is stated as the line of the latest customer-pay parts charge with every customer-pay parts and labor charge on it. Probe: a second customer-pay labor row on RO 261030 leaves the comeback credit at 645.54 (line A listed first). F4: the redemption's held_points_rule reads its own enrollment_age_months binding.
